# Puppeteer 25.10 API Migration

Yantra's browser integration runs on exactly `puppeteer-core@25.10.0`. The migration preserves
saved workflows and user-visible browser behavior while making page, frame, CDP-session, listener,
and handle ownership explicit at the boundaries where browser objects can become stale.

This feature adds no browser-management command and does not install a browser for application use.

## What It Does

### Text replacement

Both deterministic fill paths replace an existing value by focusing the control and sending the
platform select-all chord: `Meta+A` on macOS and `Control+A` elsewhere. The modifier is released even
when selection fails, and Yantra then types the requested value. Pre-populated inputs, textareas,
content-editable controls, and the resolved-secret fill path therefore replace rather than append.

The old triple-click selection gesture is intentionally gone. It was not translated to Puppeteer's
`count: 3`, because that option dispatches three real clicks and can repeatedly toggle a
widget-bearing control. The replacement path dispatches no click or double-click event. An ordinary
click still dispatches one click, including when keyboard modifiers are present.

Secret fills keep their existing security boundary: resolution occurs only at execution, the fill
remains blind with no value readback, transient plaintext is zeroed after use, and completed or
failed results and saved artifacts do not contain the resolved value.

### Agent popups and tab adoption

Agent popup capture belongs to the Puppeteer `Page` that performed the action. Yantra installs the
page's permanent popup listener and, for an action declared to open a popup, its bounded waiter
before dispatching the click. Both paths share one Page-keyed capture, so the same popup is not
processed twice. Dynamically registered `window.open` handlers are covered by the permanent
listener without imposing the declared-popup wait on ordinary clicks.

Yantra waits for a newly opened `about:blank` page to reach a real URL within a bound. It retains at
most one same-site popup for possible adoption and closes cross-site, non-HTTP(S), blank, or stale
popups. The result continues to expose the established fields:

| Field                 | Meaning                                                   |
| --------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------- |
| `popup_intercepted`   | URL observed from an intercepted popup.                   |
| `popup_followable`    | Same-site popup URL eligible for policy-checked adoption. |
| `switched_to_new_tab` | URL of the popup that became the run's active page.       |

Popup discovery does not authorize navigation. Before adoption, the caller still applies URL
provenance, host/URL policy, ethics, consent, and budget checks. Yantra uses the opener URL captured
for the causing action, so a later opener redirect does not reclassify the popup. It also checks the
retained page's current URL again at adoption time; a popup that has redirected out of policy is not
adopted.

Adoption closes the opener, makes the popup the active page, invalidates references minted on the
old page, and binds fresh popup and dialog listeners to the adopted page. Declining adoption is the
default: a later navigation, click, or fill discards the unadopted page. Adoption and teardown remove
the exact callbacks owned by the old page, and page generations prevent late work from reviving
stale popup state.

### Recorder popup coverage

The recorder uses its browser-level CDP session only for `Target.*` discovery, attachment, and
detachment. Each popup and descendant popup is instrumented through the exact public child session
whose session ID and target ID match the attachment. Page and Runtime commands, recorder bindings,
preload scripts, and immediate overlay injection are never redirected to the browser session as a
fallback.

The overlay covers both an already-loaded document and future documents. Its document guard and
exact listener replacement prevent duplicate capture when immediate injection, preload injection,
and navigation overlap. Captured popup actions retain their page URL, and fill values pass through
the recorder's existing redactor before partial or final drafts are persisted.

Child-session lookup is bounded to five seconds. An unavailable or mismatched session, destroyed
target, disconnected transport, or failed overlay installation produces one sanitized
`recording_degraded` event for that popup and no false `popup_attached` event. This is degraded
coverage, not a substitute attachment: the main recording remains usable, while actions from the
unavailable popup may be absent.

### Session-local frame tokens

The injected locator host represents the main frame as `main`. Each attached non-main Puppeteer
`Frame` receives an opaque token unique to that host. The token is stable for the same live Frame
object, including across its navigation, but two same-name or same-URL siblings still receive
different tokens.

Resolution accepts only tokens minted by the same host for a frame still present in that page's
current frame set. Foreign, detached, and replaced frames are rejected; Yantra does not guess by
URL or frame name and does not read Puppeteer's private frame ID.

Frame tokens exist only in the live locator session. They are not stored in workflow YAML,
recording metadata, or run artifacts. Existing saved workflows require no frame-token migration and
are not rewritten.

### Resource cleanup

The migration preserves and verifies these ownership guarantees:

- popup and dialog callbacks are removed from retired agent pages, declared-popup timers are
  cancelled, and pending capture work is drained during teardown;
- recorder listeners are removed by their original function references, owned popup sessions are
  detached after failed instrumentation or target closure, and stop or abort awaits idempotent
  recorder cleanup before browser shutdown;
- a composed-tree scan disposes every intermediate and untransferred JavaScript handle on partial
  failure, while successfully returned element handles remain live for their caller to own; and
- screenshot capture continues through a page-scoped CDP session, detaches that session in cleanup,
  removes Yantra's temporary marks on success or failure, and does not change viewport dimensions.

These guarantees concern page/CDP/listener/handle resources. Broader browser-process exit proof,
profile rollback, managed installation, selection, compatibility checks, and updates are outside
this feature.

## How to Use It

No new syntax is required. Existing agentic and saved-workflow commands use the migrated driver and
behavior automatically:

```console
yantra do "fill the existing form fields and continue"
yantra run <workflow-name>
```

There is currently no public recorder or annotation CLI command. Integrators using the core
`RecordingSession` API should consume `popup_attached`, `popup_closed`, and `recording_degraded`
events as coverage signals and must not interpret popup discovery as navigation authorization.

Maintainers can verify the migration with the dedicated no-LLM browser suites. CI performs this on
Windows, macOS, and Linux; Linux runs visible recorder coverage under Xvfb.

## Inputs and Outputs

Workflow schemas, recording schemas, and run-artifact formats are unchanged. Saved-workflow replay
keeps its byte-compatible result boundary. The only deliberate input-simulation difference is the
non-pointer select-all gesture before text typing.

Agent popup result fields retain their existing names and meanings. Recorder drafts continue to
store fill values as `<redacted>`, while a popup attachment failure is surfaced as a sanitized
`recording_degraded` event containing target identity and cause rather than raw binding payloads or
page data.

Frame tokens are opaque strings for internal live resolution. They are not supported workflow or
artifact inputs and must not be persisted by integrations.

## Configuration and Permissions

There are no new user settings, runtime environment variables, permissions, or CLI flags. Core
pins `puppeteer-core` to `25.10.0`; `@puppeteer/browsers@3.2.2` is used here by the migration test
provisioner.

The required CI job provisions the fixed Chrome for Testing build `152.0.7977.75` into an isolated,
test-owned cache and passes its exact executable path to the migration suites. The fixture and its
`YANTRA_TEST_BROWSER_PATH` and `YANTRA_TEST_BROWSER_MANIFEST` variables are test-only. They do not
install, select, configure, or update a browser for Yantra users.

Existing security and permission boundaries remain in force. Popup adoption stays policy-checked;
recorded values stay redacted; credentials and raw page payloads are not logged. Screenshot capture
still requires the explicit Vision Assist grant and all existing model-capability, budget,
sensitive-screen, audit, and zero-LLM checks. Screenshots are raw, unmasked pixels that bypass text
sanitization and may be sent to the configured model provider and retained in the run directory and
raw provider session log.

## Limitations

- Yantra does not gain managed browser installation, browser source selection, compatibility
  probing, a `yantra browser` command, or update handling from this migration.
- The CI Chrome for Testing fixture is proof infrastructure, not a runtime browser distribution or
  a promise that user browsers are installed automatically.
- A recorder popup whose exact child session cannot be established is deliberately omitted from
  capture after the bounded degraded event; Yantra never instruments an approximate session.
- At most one unadopted agent popup is retained. Cross-site and non-HTTP(S) popups are closed, and
  adoption remains subject to the existing policy gates.
- Frame tokens expire with their live frame and host. They cannot be reused across sessions or
  reconstructed from frame URLs or names.
- Vision pixels remain outside the text sanitizer. This migration strengthens screenshot resource
  cleanup but does not weaken or replace the existing raw-pixel consent and audit boundary.
